rule: A role is a placeholder that gets no permissions until a card is assigned. The cards assigned will define page access and read write permissions. It's that simple and there are to be zero exceptions to this rule. (Lutan, 2026-10-24)
how: scripts/check-hard-coded-security.mjs asserts ZERO (docs/decisions/2026-10-25-no-coded-security-inventory.md). There are no baselines. stillDecidesAccess names each surviving rule (file + exact text) with a backlog item; while any is listed the check prints NOT CLEAN and never prints the clean line. notAccess says why a role read is not an access rule. A record whose text is gone fails the check until it is deleted.

diagnostics.reason: tileBlock() evaluates the existing rules (OUTSIDE_REGISTRY, routes.ts) only to REPORT which one refused a held card, so the Who-does-what screen can name it. It creates no rule and grants or denies nothing. Surfacing hidden security is the point (Lutan: "I can't fix it if I can't see it"). The exemption is by function, not by file or directory: a rule added anywhere else in tiles.ts, or in src/lib/permissions/, is still counted. Added with #915 cards-grants-app.

outsideTheCardSystem.what: Admin: access to everything, hard-coded. src/lib/permissions/can.ts returns true for a login whose roles.is_admin is set before it looks at any cell or card.
outsideTheCardSystem.why: Lutan, 2026-10-25, asked directly: "I am happy for admin access = all to be hard coded." and "It should sit outside the card system." The invariant: "Admin always has access to everything. No matter what cards exist or don't exist." Measured on production 2026-10-25: Admin holds NO cards, so that one line is the only source of Admin's access; removing it would lock the only administrator out of Settings > Who does what, the screen needed to give Admin cards again. A one-way door.
rules: Admin is outside the card system, not an exception inside it.
It is not debt: no baseline, no count, never ratcheted.
It is not a precedent: Admin only, all-or-nothing.

notAccess.reason: Settings → Security is Admin-only and needs the authenticator app. These lines decide which logins a new admin may be set up for, that Admin and the public viewer cannot be an additional role (a database trigger says the same) (a doctor record can now be linked to any login: the doctor-role test was removed 2026-10-27). They guard identities on an Admin screen; none gives a card-only login anything.

Only which roles the Admin-only Security list offers as an additional role (the public viewer is never one; a database trigger says the same). Admin is read from the role's is_admin flag, and Link a doctor record is offered on every login. The server actions behind it decide, and they are Admin-only.
The order roles are listed in the Security role picker; reading the role list to fill it.
The Admin-only editing actions (Admin, aal2). Reading a role's id and kind, and saving the show-menu switch.

Draws a role's board from the roles table with the service role, after the page's own gate. The gate itself is the first entry under stillDecidesAccess (Management by role key); what is drawn is the same for either viewer.
The order roles are listed on the Who does what screen (management first, doctor last). Ordering only.
A group tile opens the page of a group on one of the roles the login HOLDS (Admin may preview any). It shows the login its own role's cards, drawn with its own permissions; it grants nothing.
Which role's board the Admin desk view opens first. Admin only; ordering.
Admin's preview of another role's home: the Admin role has no board to preview, so it goes to /admin. The page is refused to everyone but Admin (`if (!mine?.isAdmin) refuseFor(mine)`).
Lists roles for the Admin preview (management first), builds the Permissions the preview draws a role with, and reads a role's cards by its id.

roles.show_menu decides whether a login sees the left-hand menu or tiles only. It does not close a page: every page still opens from its tile or its link. Set on Settings → Who does what. NOT access, but it changes what a card-only login SEES; listed so a card test is not surprised by it. Every role is true on dev today.
Leaves the Admin role out of the list of 'who can approve photos' it prints, because Admin holds no cards. Display only.
A role's landing path is read into Permissions. Nothing redirects on it (src/app/home/page.tsx says so); the sign-in lands on /home.
Who the status-alert email goes to: the Admin logins. A recipient list, not an access rule.

noLivePolicyDeliberate._about: Triage of the table-policy-commands check (2026-10-28, docs/decisions/2026-10-28-policy-triage-1.md). A command listed here has no live policy ON PURPOSE: row security refuses it for every signed-in login, Admin included. Not access that is granted, so the hard-coded-security check does not read this; it is the record that someone read each one. Do NOT add a policy to a row here: that is a widening.

databaseHalf.what: The database no longer reads any role column to grant or deny anything (migration 0259, docs/decisions/2026-10-25-security-database-half.md).
databaseHalf.why: This registry counts lines in src/**/*.ts(x) only, so a database rule can never appear in it. The database half is recorded here so nobody concludes from a green run that the database was ever covered.
databaseHalf.listGrew: The brief named eleven. Reading the LIVE definitions rather than grepping for create-or-replace found four more: holds_app_role() (which had already moved from roles.opens_app to r.key <> public_viewer), my_permissions(), photos_medical_only() and reassign_recurring_job(). sees_all_translations(), which the brief named, does not exist.
databaseHalf.measured: No losses. Every measured change was a role reading MORE: the role columns sat beside a card check and only ever subtracted. 33 widenings across five roles, 103 surfaces unchanged, Admin unchanged on every surface. Held in docs/card-access-faults.md for Card review 2.
databaseHalf.leftInPlace: Dropped by migration 0264 (2026-10-25) together with the seven stub functions: roles.scope_residents, scope_clinical, scope_contacts, scope_photos and opens_app no longer exist.
